title: Popescu's local problem is resolvable at a regular prime with separable residue field
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $A$ a $k$-algebra of finite presentation, $\alpha:A\to\Lambda$ a homomorphism of $k$-algebras and $\mathfrak q\subset\Lambda$ a prime ideal, and let $\mathfrak h_A=\sqrt{H_{A/k}\Lambda}$ be as in [def-weil-pbc-popescu-resolution]. Assume (1) $\Lambda$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; (2) $\mathfrak q$ is minimal over $\mathfrak h_A$ (a minimal element of the set of primes of $\Lambda$ containing $\mathfrak h_A$); (3) the localization $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]; (4) the residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak q)=\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$, a field extension of $k$ via $k\to\Lambda$, is separable over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]. Then $k\to A\to\Lambda\supset\mathfrak q$ can be resolved [def-weil-pbc-popescu-resolution].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07FE (lemma-resolve-special), Section 07FB (section-separable); its proof uses Lemmas lemma-find-sequence, lemma-ogoma, lemma-desingularize-lifting-apply and the local tricks of Section 07F6

proof.text: (Generators of $H_{A/k}$ and the exponent $n$.) $k$ is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and $k$) and $A$ is of finite type over $k$, so $A$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] and $H_{A/k}$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal] is generated by finitely many elements $a_1,\dots,a_r$ ($r\ge0$). Put $I=H_{A/k}\Lambda=(\alpha(a_1),\dots,\alpha(a_r))\Lambda$, so $\mathfrak h_A=\sqrt I$ [def-weil-pbc-popescu-resolution]. By (2), $I\subset\mathfrak h_A\subset\mathfrak q$. $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a Noetherian local ring [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. A prime of $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ containing $I\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is $\mathfrak q'\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ for a prime $\mathfrak q'\subset\mathfrak q$ of $\Lambda$ containing $I$, hence containing $\sqrt I=\mathfrak h_A$; by minimality (2) $\mathfrak q'=\mathfrak q$. So $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is the only prime containing $I\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$, hence $\sqrt{I\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}}=\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq], and as $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is finitely generated there is $n\ge1$ with $\mathfrak q^n\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}\subset I\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ [lem-weil-pbc-fg-ideal-radical-power]. (Stacks chooses $n$ with $\mathfrak q^n\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}\subset\mathfrak h_A\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ and later applies Lemma 07FD with $I=\mathfrak h_A$; that only gives $\pi_i^n\in\mathfrak h_A$, while the map $B\to\Lambda$ of step 8 needs $\pi_i^n\in H_{A/k}\Lambda$. Taking $I=H_{A/k}\Lambda$ here repairs this. Stacks also writes $H_{A/R}$ for $H_{A/k}$.) Let $d=\dim\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$; by (3) $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is generated by $d$ elements [def-weil-regular-scheme].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FE (lemma-resolve-special, lines 2352-2432), first two sentences ('Set d = dim Lambda_q', 'Choose n > 0 such that ...', 'Choose generators a_1, ..., a_r of H_{A/R}')

proof.text: (The case $d=0$.) If $d=0$ then $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}=0$, so $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}=\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ is a field, separable over $k$ by (4) [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]. Hence $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is a filtered colimit of smooth $k$-algebras [lem-kun-separable-smooth-colimit] (in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-smooth-algebras]: the smooth $k$-subalgebras with the inclusions form such a diagram), and the map $A\to\Lambda\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ from the finitely presented $k$-algebra $A$ factors as $A\to B'\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ with $B'$ a smooth $k$-algebra [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-algebra-factors-filtered-colimit]. As $B'=B'_1$ is smooth, $1\in H_{B'/k}$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal], so $\mathfrak h_{B'}=\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$, which contains the ideal $\mathfrak h_{A}$ formed in $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ and is not contained in $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$: this is a resolution of $k\to A\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}\supset\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-popescu-resolution]. Here the inverse image of $\mathfrak q$ in $k$ is $\mathfrak p=0$, $k_{\mathfrak p}=k$ and $A_{\mathfrak p}=A$. Since $\mathfrak q$ is minimal over $\mathfrak h_A$ and $\dim\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}=0$, [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-delocalize-height-zero] (with $R=k$) shows that $k\to A\to\Lambda\supset\mathfrak q$ can be resolved. (Stacks' proof does not treat $d=0$ separately; there Lemma 07F8, which needs $r\ge1$, is applied with $r=d$.) From now on $d\ge1$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FE (lemma-resolve-special, lines 2352-2432), last paragraph (the same argument as its d >= 1 case, written out by the worker for d = 0)

proof.text: (The algebra $B$.) Let $R=k[x_1,\dots,x_d]$ and $B=A[x_1,\dots,x_d,z_{ij}]/(x_i^n-\sum_{j=1}^rz_{ij}a_j)_{i=1,\dots,d}$ with $rd$ variables $z_{ij}$, an $A$-algebra and an $R$-algebra via $x_i\mapsto x_i$. If $A\cong k[t_1,\dots,t_N]/(g_1,\dots,g_M)$ and $\tilde a_j\in k[t]$ lift $a_j$, then $B\cong R[t,z_{ij}]/(g_1,\dots,g_M,x_i^n-\sum_jz_{ij}\tilde a_j)$, so $B$ is an $R$-algebra of finite presentation.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FE (lemma-resolve-special, lines 2352-2432), definition of B

proof.text:
($B_{a_l}$ and $B_{x_i}$ are smooth over $R$.) Fix $l$. In $B_{a_l}$ the relations can be solved for $z_{il}=a_l^{-1}(x_i^n-\sum_{j
e l}z_{ij}a_j)$, so $B_{a_l}\cong A_{a_l}[x_1,\dots,x_d][z_{ij}:j
e l]=(A_{a_l}\otimes_kR)[z_{ij}:j
e l]$ (the inverse maps $z_{il}$ to that expression). $A_{a_l}$ is smooth over $k$ because $a_l\in H_{A/k}$ [lem-weil-pbc-singular-ideal-localization-smooth]; hence $A_{a_l}\otimes_kR$ is smooth over $R$ (base change), the polynomial ring over it is smooth over it [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-smooth], and the composite $R	o B_{a_l}$ is smooth [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition]. Now fix $i$. In $B_{x_i}$ the element $x_i^n=\sum_jz_{ij}a_j$ is a unit, so $a_1,\dots,a_r$ generate the unit ideal of $B_{x_i}$ (if $r=0$, $B_{x_i}=0$); each $(B_{x_i})_{a_j}=(B_{a_j})_{x_i}$ is smooth over $R$ [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-principal-localization], hence $B_{x_i}$ is smooth over $R$ [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-local-on-cover].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FE (lemma-resolve-special, lines 2352-2432), 'Each B_{a_j} is smooth over R ... Hence B_{x_i} is smooth over R' (Stacks: 'A_{a_j} is smooth over k'; the base change and the covering argument are written out)

proof.text: (The algebra $C$ and the exponent $c$.) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-improve-presentation] to the finitely presented $R$-algebra $B$: there are a $B$-algebra $C$ of finite type and a $B$-algebra retraction $\rho:C\to B$ such that $C_b$ is smooth over $R$ with $\Omega_{C_b/R}$ free whenever $B_b$ is smooth over $R$. $C$ is of finite type over $R$ ($B$ is), so of finite presentation over the Noetherian ring $R$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian, lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation]. By step 4, $C_{x_i}$ ($i=1,\dots,d$) and $C_{a_j}$ ($j=1,\dots,r$) are smooth over $R$, and $\Omega_{C_{x_i}/R}$ is free. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-free-differentials-strictly-standard-power] there are $e_0(i)$ with $x_i^{c}$ strictly standard in $C$ over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-strictly-standard-element] for $c\ge e_0(i)$; take $c=\max_ie_0(i)$, so every $x_i^c$ is strictly standard in $C$ over $R$. Put $e=8c$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FE (lemma-resolve-special, lines 2352-2432), 'Let B -> C be the R-algebra map constructed in Lemma 07CE ... we can find c > 0 such that x_i^c is strictly standard in C/R, see Lemma 07EZ'

proof.text: (The elements $\pi_i$ and the maps to $\Lambda$.) By step 1 and (1), (3), [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-find-sequence] applies to $\Lambda$, $I=H_{A/k}\Lambda\subset\mathfrak q$, $n$ and $e=8c$: there are $\pi_1,\dots,\pi_d\in\Lambda$ with (i) $(\pi_1,\dots,\pi_d)\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}=\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$, (ii) $\pi_i^n\in I$, (iii) $\mathrm{Ann}_{M_i}(\pi_i)=\mathrm{Ann}_{M_i}(\pi_i^2)$ on $M_i=\Lambda/(\pi_1^e,\dots,\pi_{i-1}^e)\Lambda$. By (ii) write $\pi_i^n=\sum_j\lambda_{ij}\alpha(a_j)$ with $\lambda_{ij}\in\Lambda$ (Stacks writes $\pi_{ij}$ once for $\lambda_{ij}$). Make $\Lambda$ an $R$-algebra by the $k$-algebra map $x_i\mapsto\pi_i$; the $A$-algebra map $\beta:B\to\Lambda$, $x_i\mapsto\pi_i$, $z_{ij}\mapsto\lambda_{ij}$, is well defined (the relations map to $\pi_i^n-\sum_j\lambda_{ij}\alpha(a_j)=0$) and $R$-linear, and $\gamma=\beta\circ\rho:C\to\Lambda$ is an $R$-algebra map with $\gamma|_B=\beta$, so $A\to B\to C\xrightarrow{\gamma}\Lambda$ composes to $\alpha$. By (i) $\pi_i/1\in\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$, so $\pi_i\in\mathfrak q$ ($\mathfrak q$ prime); thus the inverse image $\mathfrak p$ of $\mathfrak q$ in $R$ contains $x_1,\dots,x_d$, and since $(x_1,\dots,x_d)$ is maximal ($R/(x)=k$), $\mathfrak p=(x_1,\dots,x_d)$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FE (lemma-resolve-special, lines 2352-2432), 'Now choose pi_1, ..., pi_d as in Lemma 07FD ... There is a map B -> Lambda given by x_i -> pi_i and z_ij -> lambda_ij'

proof.text: (Reduction modulo $x^e$ by Lemma 07F8.) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-lift-solution] to the Noetherian ring $R$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], $R\to C\xrightarrow{\gamma}\Lambda\supset\mathfrak q$ and the elements $x_1^c,\dots,x_d^c\in R$ ($r=d\ge1$), which map to $\pi_i^c\in\mathfrak q$; note $(x_i^c)^8=x_i^e\mapsto\pi_i^e$. Hypothesis (2) is step 5. Hypothesis (1) for $R$: $R/(x_1^e,\dots,x_{i-1}^e)\cong(k[x_1,\dots,x_{i-1}]/(x_1^e,\dots,x_{i-1}^e))[x_i,\dots,x_d]$ is a polynomial ring in $x_i$ over a ring, on which multiplication by $x_i^c$ and $x_i^{2c}$ is injective, so both annihilators are $0$. Hypothesis (1) for $\Lambda$: on $M_i$, $\mathrm{Ann}(\pi_i)=\mathrm{Ann}(\pi_i^2)$ (iii) implies $\mathrm{Ann}(\pi_i^m)=\mathrm{Ann}(\pi_i)$ for all $m\ge1$ (if $\pi_i^{m+1}y=0$ with $m\ge1$ then $\pi_i^2(\pi_i^{m-1}y)=0$, so $\pi_i(\pi_i^{m-1}y)=0$; induct), hence $\mathrm{Ann}(\pi_i^c)=\mathrm{Ann}(\pi_i^{2c})$. Therefore, with $\bar R=R/(x_1^e,\dots,x_d^e)$, $\bar C=C/(x^e)C$, $\bar\Lambda=\Lambda/(\pi_1^e,\dots,\pi_d^e)\Lambda$, $\bar{\mathfrak q}=\mathfrak q/(\pi^e)\Lambda$: if $\bar R\to\bar C\to\bar\Lambda\supset\bar{\mathfrak q}$ can be resolved, then $R\to C\to\Lambda\supset\mathfrak q$ can be resolved.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FE (lemma-resolve-special, lines 2352-2432), 'Now we apply Lemma 07F8 to R -> C -> Lambda ⊃ q and the sequence x_1^c, ..., x_d^c ... Thus it suffices to resolve R/(x^e) -> C/(x^e) -> Lambda/(pi^e) ⊃ q/(pi^e) for e = 8c'

proof.text: (A resolution over $R$ gives one over $k$.) Stacks passes over this point. Let $C\to D\to\Lambda$ be a resolution of $R\to C\to\Lambda\supset\mathfrak q$: $D$ of finite presentation over $R$, $\mathfrak h_C^{R}\subset\mathfrak h_D^{R}\not\subset\mathfrak q$, where $\mathfrak h^R$ is formed with singular ideals over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-popescu-resolution]. $D$ is of finite presentation over $k$ ($R$ is). If $D_g$ is smooth over $R$ it is smooth over $k$, since $R=k[x]$ is smooth over $k$ [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-smooth, lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition]; so $H_{D/R}\subset H_{D/k}$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal] and $\mathfrak h_D^R\subset\mathfrak h_D^k$, whence $\mathfrak h_D^k\not\subset\mathfrak q$. By step 5, $C_{a_j}$ is smooth over $R$, so the image of $a_j$ in $C$ lies in $H_{C/R}$, and $\gamma(a_j)=\alpha(a_j)$; hence $H_{A/k}\Lambda=(\alpha(a_j))_j\subset H_{C/R}\Lambda$ and $\mathfrak h_A=\mathfrak h_A^k\subset\mathfrak h_C^R\subset\mathfrak h_D^R\subset\mathfrak h_D^k$. So $A\to B\to C\to D\to\Lambda$ is a resolution of $k\to A\to\Lambda\supset\mathfrak q$. It therefore suffices to resolve $\bar R\to\bar C\to\bar\Lambda\supset\bar{\mathfrak q}$ (step 7).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FE (lemma-resolve-special, lines 2352-2432) (gap in the source: Lemma 07F8 yields a resolution over R = k[x_1..x_d], the statement asks for one over k; argument written by the worker)

proof.text: (Reduction to the localization by Lemma 07FA.) $\bar R$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], $\bar C$ is of finite presentation over $\bar R$, and $\bar\Lambda$ is an $\bar R$-algebra. The inverse image of $\bar{\mathfrak q}$ in $\bar R$ is $\bar{\mathfrak p}=\mathfrak p/(x^e)$, and $\bar R_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}=R_{\mathfrak p}/(x^e)R_{\mathfrak p}$, $\bar C_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}=C_{\mathfrak p}/(x^e)C_{\mathfrak p}$, $\bar\Lambda_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}=\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}/(\pi_1^e,\dots,\pi_d^e)\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ (localization commutes with quotients). A prime of $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ containing all $\pi_i^e$ contains all $\pi_i$, hence $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ by (i); so $\bar\Lambda_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$ has exactly one prime: $\dim\bar\Lambda_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}=0$. If $\mathfrak h_{\bar C}\not\subset\bar{\mathfrak q}$, the identity factorization $\bar C\to\bar C\to\bar\Lambda$ is already a resolution [def-weil-pbc-popescu-resolution]. Otherwise $\mathfrak h_{\bar C}\subset\bar{\mathfrak q}$, and $\bar{\mathfrak q}$ is minimal over $\mathfrak h_{\bar C}$: a prime $\mathfrak q'\subset\bar{\mathfrak q}$ of $\bar\Lambda$ gives the prime $\mathfrak q'\bar\Lambda_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$ of $\bar\Lambda_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$, which is the unique one, so $\mathfrak q'=\bar{\mathfrak q}$. (Stacks does not check hypothesis (1) of 07FA.) By [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-delocalize-height-zero] it suffices to resolve $\bar R_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}\to\bar C_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}\to\bar\Lambda_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}\supset\bar{\mathfrak q}\bar\Lambda_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FE (lemma-resolve-special, lines 2352-2432), 'By Lemma 07FA it suffices to resolve this after localizing at q'

proof.text: (Flatness.) $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a regular local ring of dimension $d$ whose maximal ideal is generated by $x_1,\dots,x_d$, with residue field $R/\mathfrak p=k$ [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-origin-regular-local]. $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is a regular local ring of dimension $d$ whose maximal ideal is generated by $\pi_1,\dots,\pi_d$ (i), so $\pi_1,\dots,\pi_d$ is a regular sequence in $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence, def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. $R\setminus\mathfrak p$ maps into $\Lambda\setminus\mathfrak q$, so $R\to\Lambda$ induces a local homomorphism $R_{\mathfrak p}\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ of Noetherian local rings [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] sending $x_i\mapsto\pi_i$; it is flat [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-regular]. Hence $\bar\Lambda_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}=\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}/(x_1^e,\dots,x_d^e)\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat over $\bar R_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}=R_{\mathfrak p}/(x^e)R_{\mathfrak p}$ [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-quotient-flat].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FE (lemma-resolve-special, lines 2352-2432), 'since x_1, ..., x_d map to a regular sequence in Lambda_q we see that R_p -> Lambda_q is flat, see Algebra, Lemma 07DY. Hence R_p/(x^e) -> Lambda_q/(pi^e) is a flat ring map of Artinian local rings'

proof.text: (Filtered colimit of smooth algebras.) The maximal ideal $\bar{\mathfrak m}=(x_1,\dots,x_d)$ of $\bar R_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}$ is nilpotent: $\bar{\mathfrak m}^{d(e-1)+1}=0$, as every monomial of that degree is divisible by some $x_i^e$. $\bar R_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}/\bar{\mathfrak m}=R_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}=k$ and $\bar\Lambda_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}/\bar{\mathfrak m}\bar\Lambda_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}=\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}/(\pi_1,\dots,\pi_d)\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}=\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ by (i), the $k$-algebra structure being the given one ($R\to\Lambda$ is a $k$-algebra map). By (4) [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension] and [lem-kun-separable-smooth-colimit], $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ is a filtered colimit of smooth $k$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-smooth-algebras]. With step 10, [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-lift-nilpotent] applied to $\bar R_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}\to\bar\Lambda_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$ and $I=\bar{\mathfrak m}$ shows that $\bar\Lambda_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$ is a filtered colimit of smooth $\bar R_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}$-algebras.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FE (lemma-resolve-special, lines 2352-2432), 'Moreover, this map induces a separable field extension on residue fields by assumption. Thus this map is a filtered colimit of smooth algebras by Algebra, Lemma 07BV and Proposition 07CM'

proof.text: (The resolution.) $\bar C_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}$ is of finite presentation over $\bar R_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}$, so by step 11 and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-algebra-factors-filtered-colimit] the map $\bar C_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}\to\bar\Lambda_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$ factors through a smooth $\bar R_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}$-algebra $T$. Then $1\in H_{T/\bar R_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}}$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal], so $\mathfrak h_T=\bar\Lambda_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$, which contains $\mathfrak h_{\bar C_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}}$ and is not contained in $\bar{\mathfrak q}\bar\Lambda_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$: $T$ resolves $\bar R_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}\to\bar C_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}\to\bar\Lambda_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}\supset\bar{\mathfrak q}\bar\Lambda_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$ [def-weil-pbc-popescu-resolution]. By steps 9, 7 and 8, $k\to A\to\Lambda\supset\mathfrak q$ can be resolved.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FE (lemma-resolve-special, lines 2352-2432), 'Existence of the desired solution follows from Algebra, Lemma 07C3'
